question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics remain a core Doctor contribution in this stacked RFC implementation, or should the lifecycle surface be narrowed or moved to an extension-owned path before landing?
rationale: The patch is intentionally introducing a new core diagnostic capability rather than repairing an established contract, and the protected maintainer label plus open RFC/stack do not establish that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental core path
options.body: Accept the Doctor contribution as part of the experimental Claws stack, land prerequisites first, and require refreshed main-target proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the core seam
options.body: Keep only generic Doctor integration in core and move lifecycle-specific diagnostics behind an extension or plugin boundary if the RFC scope should stay lean.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer this diagnostics layer until the RFC and ownership model have explicit maintainer approval and a settled landing sequence.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental core path
recommendation.body: Accept the Doctor contribution as part of the experimental Claws stack, land prerequisites first, and require refreshed main-target proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline shows direct feature-discussion involvement; final product-boundary ownership remains low-confidence without a visible approval comment.
